subject.title: fix(agents): prevent opaque shell commands bypassing auto-review

question: Should automatic approval fail closed for PowerShell startup, remoting, encoded-command, and other opaque carriers even when that adds human-approval prompts to existing auto-mode workflows?
rationale: The implementation is a narrow extension of the merged shell-startup boundary, but the compatibility tradeoff is intentional security policy and the PR carries the protected maintainer label.

options.title: Confirm the stricter approval boundary
options.body: Accept the added prompts for opaque carriers, contingent on current-head host-level proof and direct validation that Codex Guardian semantics remain unchanged.

options.title: Narrow the carrier policy
options.body: Keep automatic review for any specifically identified carrier that maintainers can prove exposes a fully faithful reviewed command without startup or remoting side effects.

recommendation.title: Confirm the stricter approval boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the added prompts for opaque carriers, contingent on current-head host-level proof and direct validation that Codex Guardian semantics remain unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged predecessor and this follow-up both place this person closest to the established auto-review security boundary.
